Install back cut (dovetail modified) Stage 1 and 2 turbine blades at next scheduled maintenance (HGPI or MI)

our_value: For units operating in high ambient and/or humid/corrosive conditions: perform routine turbine wheel inspections at intervals based on installed configuration (shot peening condition at first fire, cooling slot geometry, material heat treatment, balance rail & lock wire tab configuration) per Tables 1–6.

Stage 1 & Stage 2 wheel dovetail Eddy Current Inspection (ECI): perform at the frequency defined in the applicable configuration table (Tables 1–6) and continue until rotor retirement; ECI is available and recommended for all wheel posts identified in Tables 1 and 2.
If cooling slot crack is detected during inspection: immediate wheel replacement will be recommended to help avoid the risk of wheel post liberation during operation.

Visual inspection (VT) / borescope inspection (BI): for non-shot peened rotors, perform visual inspection of all exposed turbine rotor surfaces when available; observe/borescope accessible rotor surfaces and examine broach slot fillets/slot bottoms/tangs/cooling slots, cooling slots in wheel broach slots, spacer rim seal tooth rubs/coating, balance weights (looseness/migration/staking quality/set screw), nut damage/surface indications in flanges and webs.
Ultrasonic testing (UT): inspect counterbore outside diameter ligaments on distance piece and turbine aft shaft.

Fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI): inspect staked balance weight grooves at all major inspection intervals and when the CDC is removed during a Hot Gas Path inspection; inspect lock wire tab fillets when turbine blades are removed during routine maintenance intervals; do not use FPI for wheel posts.

Stage 3 turbine wheel (TW3) balance weight grooves: if staked, FPI every Major Inspection (MI) and when the Exhaust Frame is removed during Hot Gas Path Inspection (HGPI); if stakeless, no inspections necessary.
Stage 3 turbine wheel (TW3) lockwire tabs: if original, FPI every HGPI while buckets are removed; if modified, FPI every MI.
Turbine aft shaft (TAS) balance weight grooves: if staked, FPI every MI and when the Exhaust Frame is removed during HGPI; if stakeless, no inspections necessary.

Install dovetail modified ('back cut') Stage 1 and Stage 2 turbine blades on all turbine rotors; apply at the next scheduled maintenance (HGPI or MI) and ensure inventory parts are modified during standard repair/refurbishment by a GE Vernova Service Center.

Cleaning prerequisite for ECI: prior to ECI, appropriately clean turbine rotor (preferred dry ice/CO2 blasting; acceptable hand-cleaning if CO2 blast not available) to facilitate proper functioning of ECI equipment and accurate readings.

Perform recommended NDT inspections (ECI/Visual/BI/FPI/UT) per Tables 1–6 based on installed wheel configuration (heat treatment, peening condition, cooling slot geometry, balance rail & lock wire tab).

Perform ECI every 48 khrs or 2,400 starts for 2 Step Age wheels with original cooling slot that were never fired without shot peening (every 24 khrs or 900 starts if back cut buckets not installed)
Perform ECI at 96 khrs or 3,600 starts for 2 Step Age Stage 1 wheels with contoured or enhanced cooling slot (every 48 khrs or 2,400 starts if back cut buckets not installed for contoured)

Perform BI every HGPI when CDC is not removed for applicable Stage 1 wheels
Perform FPI on LWT every HGPI when buckets are removed; on BWG every Major and when CDC is removed during HGPI
For stakeless & modified tab wheels: FPI LWT every Major only
For 3 Step Age wheels: FPI LWT every Major only
Install back cut (modified) turbine blades on all turbine rotors at next scheduled maintenance
TW3 staked BWG: FPI every MI and when Exhaust Frame is removed during HGPI; stakeless: no inspections necessary
TW3 original LWT: FPI every HGPI while buckets are removed; modified LWT: FPI every MI
TAS staked BWG: FPI every MI and when Exhaust Frame is removed during HGPI; stakeless: no inspections necessary
Contact GE Vernova representative for peening modification wheels to determine applicable peening condition based on turbine serial number
If cooling slot crack is detected, immediate wheel replacement is recommended to avoid risk of wheel post liberation during operation

our_value: Determine installed Stage 1 and Stage 2 wheel configuration (material heat treatment, shot peening condition at first fire, cooling slot geometry, balance rail & lock wire tab) and follow the applicable inspection methods and intervals in Tables 1–6.

If peening condition is uncertain for wheels listed as 'Peening Modification': contact GE Vernova representative with turbine (or rotor) serial number to determine applicable peening condition; until validated, assume 'Fired without Shot Peening' recommendations apply.
Stage 1 & Stage 2 wheel posts/dovetails: perform dovetail ECI at the frequency defined in Tables 1–6 (recommended until rotor retirement).

Perform Visual inspection and borescope inspection (BI) of accessible rotor surfaces when available; for non-shot peened rotors, visual inspection of all exposed turbine rotor surfaces is recommended.
Perform UT on 'counterbore outside diameter ligaments on distance piece and turbine aft shaft' as part of recommended inspection features.
Perform FPI for cracks on balance weights and lockwire tabs per the intervals in Tables 1–6 and the FPI guidance (note: FPI is not recommended for wheel posts).
If a cooling slot crack is detected during inspection, immediately replace the wheel (recommended) to avoid risk of wheel post liberation during operation.

Stage 3 turbine wheel (TW3) balance weight grooves: if staked, perform FPI every Major Inspection (MI) and when the Exhaust Frame is removed during Hot Gas Path Inspection (HGPI); if stakeless, no inspections necessary.
Stage 3 turbine wheel (TW3) lockwire tabs: if original, perform FPI every HGPI while buckets are removed; if modified, perform FPI every MI.
Turbine aft shaft (TAS) balance weight grooves: if staked, perform FPI every MI and when the Exhaust Frame is removed during HGPI; if stakeless, no inspections necessary.
Rotor preparation for ECI: clean rotor prior to ECI (preferred dry ice/CO2 blasting; ensure surfaces free of oil beforehand; hand-cleaning acceptable if CO2 blast not available).

Install back cut (dovetail modified) Stage 1 and 2 turbine blades on all turbine rotors; apply at next scheduled maintenance (HGPI or MI) and ensure inventory parts receive back-cut modification via GE Vernova Service Center.

our_value: Send affected spare sets of S3Ss to a GE Vernova Service Center to receive the cooling air modification prior to installation/operation.

After installation of modified S3Ss, implement required configuration changes: resize ninth-stage extraction air orifice plate; update unit control constant; install updated inter-segment seals (laminate seals) on Stage 1 Shroud, Stage 2 Nozzle, Stage 2 Shroud, Stage 3 Nozzle, Stage 3 Shroud.
Send affected S3Bs (that operated with affected/uncooled S3Ss) to a GE Vernova Service Center for evaluation and to receive the new repair process (marked with machining part number 129T6911).

For limited units with S3Bs refurbished before the new repair process: perform FPI every 4000 fired hours covering both pressure and suction sides of the tip shroud fillets until removed from service.

ds_value: All affected spare sets of S3Ss should be sent to a GE Vernova Service Center to receive the cooling air modification prior to installation and operation in a unit.

After installation of modified S3Ss, install updated inter-segment seals (laminate seals) on Stage 1 Shroud, Stage 2 Nozzle, Stage 2 Shroud, Stage 3 Nozzle, and Stage 3 Shroud.
Affected S3Bs that have operated with uncooled S3Ss should be sent to a GE Vernova Service Center for evaluation and to receive the new repair process.
7F.04 Standard AGP parts repaired with the new process should only be operated with modified (cooled) S3Ss in their subsequent tour.
For 7F.04 Tech parts, eligibility for subsequent tour operation will be assessed during the repair process; if eligible, they must be operated with the modified (cooled) S3S configuration.
Parts tagged 129T6911P0001 through P048 and 129T6911P0101 through P0108 are limited to ONLY one tour after repair and must be scrapped after completion of that tour.

S3Bs previously refurbished before the new repair process was implemented should be Fluorescent Penetrant inspected (FPI) every 4000 fired hours until removed from service, covering both pressure and suction sides of the tip shroud fillets.
A CM&U process is mandatory to implement the S3S cooling modification and associated configuration changes.
our_value: S3S cooling modification: send all affected spare sets of S3Ss (Table 1 affected part numbers) to a GE Vernova Service Center for cooling air modification prior to installation and operation.

S3S cooling modification: send all affected S3Ss currently operating in a unit (Table 1 affected part numbers) to a GE Vernova Service Center for cooling air modification after completion of current tour.

Post-S3S modification configuration changes (required to meet TIL): resize ninth-stage extraction air orifice plate; update unit control constant; install updated inter-segment seals (laminate seals) on Stage 1 Shroud, Stage 2 Nozzle, Stage 2 Shroud, Stage 3 Nozzle, and Stage 3 Shroud (laminate seals not required for Stage 1 Nozzles).

S3B evaluation/repair: for S3Bs that have operated with affected (uncooled) S3Ss per Table 1, send S3Bs to a GE Vernova Service Center for evaluation and to receive the new repair process; repaired parts will be marked with machining part number 129T6911.
Parts tour restriction (Standard AGP): 7F.04 Standard AGP parts repaired with the new process must only be operated with modified (cooled) S3Ss in the subsequent tour.
Parts tour restriction (Tech): for 7F.04 Tech parts, eligibility for subsequent tour operation is assessed during repair; if eligible, they must be operated with modified (cooled) S3Ss.

One-tour-after-repair limit: parts tagged 129T6911P0001 through P048 and 129T6911P0101 through P0108 are limited to only one tour after repair; after completion of one tour post-repair, these parts must be scrapped.

Legacy refurbished S3Bs (before new repair process): perform Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (FPI) every 4000 fired hours until removed from service; FPI to cover both pressure and suction sides of the tip shroud fillets.
